topics.title: Theme I: Our environment

outcomes.text: Describe that everything around us makes up our environment.
Group the parts of the environment into living and non-living.

topics.title: Theme II: Biodiversity

outcomes.text: Recognise that animals and plants come in a huge variety of types.
Tell how animals and plants live in different environments (basic idea of habitat).

topics.title: Theme III: Human relation to the natural environment

subtopics.title: Food and where it comes from

outcomes.text: Describe the kinds of foods and drinks they consume.
Identify the sources of food items as plants or animals.

topics.title: Theme I: Causes of climate change

outcomes.text: Observe which things produce smoke and make the air dirty (vehicles, burning wood, coal, crop stubble).
Identify dust as a reason for dirty air and as a way carbon is added to the atmosphere.
Meet the term carbon footprint.

topics.title: Theme I: Responsible consumption and conservation

outcomes.text: Recognise that resources like trees, water, wildlife and energy come from nature and must be used carefully.
Explain how excessive use of resources leads to shortages.

topics.title: Theme III: Water management

outcomes.text: Explain with examples that animals, plants and humans need water for life.

topics.title: Theme IV: Sustainable lifestyle

outcomes.text: Identify walking and cycling as healthy ways to travel.

topics.title: Theme I: Social impacts of climate change

outcomes.text: Learn that floods and heat affect people's health and life, such as heat stroke and losing homes, cattle and crops.

topics.title: Theme II: Strategies for safety and resilience

outcomes.text: Learn ways people can prepare to protect themselves from heavy rain, floods and heatwaves.

topics.title: Theme III: Climate anxiety and constructive coping

outcomes.text: Identify and label basic emotions (happy, sad, scared, angry) when discussing climate and nature.
Describe simple mindfulness techniques like breathing exercises to manage emotions.

topics.title: Theme IV: Community action

outcomes.text: Identify climate action that can be done at school with peers: planting, gardening, waste management, saving water, avoiding food waste.

topics.title: Theme I: Our environment

subtopics.title: Living and non-living need each other

outcomes.text: Describe how living and non-living things in our surroundings need each other.
Share what humans need around them to make their environment comfortable.

topics.title: Theme II: Biodiversity

subtopics.title: How plants and animals differ and interact

outcomes.text: Identify and contrast how animals and plants differ in behaviours and habitats.
Show how different animals interact with each other (food chain, habitat, population).

topics.title: Theme III: Human relation to the natural environment

outcomes.text: Analyse dietary habits of selected species, including plants and animals.
Describe the basic nutritional needs of humans at each stage of life.

topics.title: Theme I: Causes of climate change

outcomes.text: Tell how cutting trees affects the environment negatively.
Discuss ways to increase plants and trees.

topics.title: Theme I: Responsible consumption and conservation

outcomes.text: Differentiate basic needs from wants and analyse how consumption affects the environment.
Analyse how cutting trees, hunting and wasting water harm the environment using local examples.

topics.title: Theme III: Water management

outcomes.text: Recognise fresh water as key to human life.
Identify freshwater sources available at school and home.

topics.title: Theme IV: Sustainable lifestyle

outcomes.text: Describe how food packaging can contribute to waste.

topics.title: Theme I: Social impacts of climate change

outcomes.text: Identify the effects of no or scarce rain on schools, homes and people working outdoors such as farmers and labourers.

topics.title: Theme II: Strategies for safety and resilience

outcomes.text: Describe protection measures for areas with very low or no rain and water scarcity.

topics.title: Theme III: Climate anxiety and constructive coping

outcomes.text: Identify and label basic emotions (happy, sad, scared, angry) when discussing climate and nature.
Describe simple mindfulness techniques like breathing exercises to manage emotions.

topics.title: Theme IV: Community action

outcomes.text: Identify activities that make the home clean and green: waste management, avoiding dust and smoke, gardening.

topics.title: Theme I: Our environment

subtopics.title: Changes in living and non-living things

outcomes.text: Ask about possible changes in the quality of living and non-living things in the environment.
Observe how diverse life (plants, animals) is on Earth.

topics.title: Theme II: Biodiversity

outcomes.text: Tell about micro-organisms and their role in ecosystems, including locally.
Identify tools such as microscopes used to recognise microscopic diversity.

topics.title: Theme III: Human relation to the natural environment

outcomes.text: Compare different diets and food cultures around the world.
Discuss how urbanisation and mechanisation increase the distance food travels.

topics.title: Theme I: Causes of climate change

outcomes.text: Cite ways to reduce smoke and dust to make air clean.
Investigate how food waste harms the environment.

topics.title: Theme I: Responsible consumption and conservation

outcomes.text: Explain overconsumption and how it is shown.
Define scarcity as limited availability of resources.

topics.title: Theme III: Water management

outcomes.text: Explain the water cycle and how climate disturbs it.
Demonstrate that higher temperatures disrupt the cycle: melting glaciers, evaporation, changed rain patterns.

topics.title: Theme IV: Sustainable lifestyle

outcomes.text: Define sustainable in simple terms, such as using resources wisely.

topics.title: Theme I: Social impacts of climate change

outcomes.text: Know about smog in Pakistan and its impact on health, life and activities, such as lung disease and school closure.

topics.title: Theme II: Strategies for safety and resilience

outcomes.text: Describe measures to protect health and social and economic activities during smog, fires and smoke.

topics.title: Theme III: Climate anxiety and constructive coping

outcomes.text: Identify and label basic emotions (happy, sad, scared, angry) when discussing climate and nature.
Describe simple mindfulness techniques like breathing exercises to manage emotions.

topics.title: Theme IV: Community action

outcomes.text: Identify activities that create awareness among children to take action: drama, drawing, pamphlets, songs.

topics.title: Theme I: Our environment

outcomes.text: Identify factors that sustain life on Earth, linking biotic and abiotic elements.
Recognise that humans are part of every ecosystem.

topics.title: Theme II: Biodiversity

outcomes.text: Explain the complexity of biodiversity and ecosystems, including in the local environment.
Identify how daily activities link with plants, animals and the natural environment (food, clothes, houses).

topics.title: Theme III: Human relation to the natural environment

outcomes.text: Discuss how population increase, urbanisation and food security are linked.
Identify packing materials for food as more useful or harmful to the environment.

topics.title: Theme I: Causes of climate change

subtopics.title: Human activities that harm air, water, soil

outcomes.text: Cite human activities affecting the quality of air, water and soil.
Discuss how non-vegetarian food and lifestyle choices contribute to climate change.

topics.title: Theme II: Climate change impacts and hazards

outcomes.text: Analyse effects of climate change on local weather: heat, droughts, wildfires, uneven rainfall, storms.
Analyse effects on agriculture: unpredictable seasons, poor soil, food shortages.
Explore effects on human health, inequality, displacement and the economy.

topics.title: Theme III: Monitoring climate change

outcomes.text: Understand that environment quality is measured by indicators such as greenhouse gas levels, temperature and biodegradable content of water and soil.

topics.title: Theme I: Responsible consumption and conservation

outcomes.text: Explain how forests, wildlife and water are good for physical and mental well-being.
Describe the impact of human activities on the environment in Pakistan with local examples such as plastic waste and water scarcity.

topics.title: Theme II: Renewable energy use

outcomes.text: Analyse how higher energy use from fossil fuels increases carbon emissions and pollutes the atmosphere.
Compare renewable and non-renewable energy sources with examples and their environmental impact.

topics.title: Theme III: Water management

outcomes.text: Explain global warming threats from increasing greenhouse gases.
Use local case studies to show how global warming has made areas water scarce.
Show how untreated industrial waste contaminates canals, rivers and seas.

topics.title: Theme IV: Sustainable lifestyle

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of an ecosystem with simple examples.
Compare sustainable houses (mud, bamboo, solar-powered) by materials and energy efficiency.

topics.title: Theme I: Social impacts of climate change

outcomes.text: Describe what weather patterns and climate change are and how they affect people's lives.

topics.title: Theme II: Strategies for safety and resilience

outcomes.text: Access information and data on extreme weather and how people prepare to avoid loss of life and assets.
Identify the role youth and community play in disaster preparedness.

topics.title: Theme III: Climate anxiety and constructive coping

outcomes.text: Discuss fears and anxiety management strategies and the support needed, practising them in role play.

topics.title: Theme IV: Community action

outcomes.text: Explain why taking action with others in the community is more powerful than individual action.
Identify climate plans or actions the community has in place.

topics.title: Theme I: Our environment

outcomes.text: Identify different ecosystems with biodiversity, urban and rural.
Understand how weather, climate and seasons relate to each other.
Recognise how rainfall, temperature and sunlight changes through the year shape local biodiversity.

topics.title: Theme II: Biodiversity

outcomes.text: Describe and differentiate how specific plants (trees, forests, sea algae, plankton) matter for the environment.
Compare roles of species in an ecosystem: self-regulation, decomposers, umbrella species.

topics.title: Theme III: Human relation to the natural environment

outcomes.text: Understand the relationship between humans and nature.
Discuss how natural environments such as forests are good for human mental and physical well-being.

topics.title: Theme I: Causes of climate change

outcomes.text: Describe natural causes of climate change that have existed since Earth began.
Explore industrial manufacturing, agriculture, buildings and air traffic as human causes.

topics.title: Theme II: Climate change impacts and hazards

outcomes.text: Analyse impacts on the environment: smog, melting glaciers, rising sea levels, flooding, warmer oceans.
Analyse effects on animals: extinction risk, biodiversity crisis, altered habitats, migration.

topics.title: Theme III: Monitoring climate change

subtopics.title: Quality standards of air, water, soil

outcomes.text: Research and describe the standards of air, water and soil quality fit for life.

topics.title: Theme IV: Climate justice

outcomes.text: Visualise how pollution, drought and storms are felt everywhere but some places suffer more.
Explain how wealthy populations, industrialised countries and polluting companies are more responsible for climate change.

topics.title: Theme I: Responsible consumption and conservation

outcomes.text: Explain how natural resources are not infinite; fossil fuel, plants and animals exist in finite amounts.
Explain the principles of the 4Rs: Refuse, Re-use, Repair, Recycle.

topics.title: Theme II: Renewable energy use

outcomes.text: Analyse sources of energy used at home and assess if free renewable sources (solar, wind, water, biomass, geothermal) are available.

topics.title: Theme III: Water management

outcomes.text: Explain, using the water cycle, how fresh water is a scarce resource.
Collect evidence of water storage methods and what water conservation means.

topics.title: Theme IV: Sustainable lifestyle

outcomes.text: Identify green spaces (parks, gardens, forests) and blue spaces (lakes, rivers, oceans).

topics.title: Theme I: Social impacts of climate change

outcomes.text: Identify how climate change affects physical and mental health, economy and relationships.

topics.title: Theme II: Strategies for safety and resilience

outcomes.text: Collect information on preparatory activities by government and other organisations to prepare communities.

topics.title: Theme III: Climate anxiety and constructive coping

outcomes.text: Research and discuss strategies that help others manage climate change-related anxiety.

topics.title: Theme IV: Community action

outcomes.text: Identify actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions at school: reduce food waste, walk, plant-based diet, conserve energy.

topics.title: Theme I: Our environment

outcomes.text: Describe Earth's layers: geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere.

topics.title: Theme II: Biodiversity

outcomes.text: Describe tectonic plates and how they cause changes in species in different world regions.
Discuss how Earth's atmospheric composition has evolved.
Analyse changes in biotic and abiotic elements that cause migration and affect biodiversity.

topics.title: Theme III: Human relation to the natural environment

outcomes.text: Compare environmental impacts of different modes of transportation.
Describe how intensive and industrial fishing harms marine ecosystems.
Describe the link between pollution and changing weather patterns leading to climate change.

topics.title: Theme I: Causes of climate change

outcomes.text: Investigate what greenhouse gases are and how they become a reason for climate change.
Explore ways to reduce carbon footprint.

topics.title: Theme II: Climate change impacts and hazards

outcomes.text: Identify climate-induced disasters happening in Pakistan and their impacts on life.
Imagine a future with climate change: higher temperatures, health issues, biodiversity change.
Describe the concept of climate action.

topics.title: Theme III: Monitoring climate change

outcomes.text: Demonstrate methods of measuring air quality (AQI) and the tools or apps used.
Demonstrate how water and soil quality assessment is done and with what tools.

topics.title: Theme IV: Climate justice

outcomes.text: Identify ways climate change disproportionately affects girls, women, children with disabilities, refugees, Indigenous communities, informal workers and poorer countries.

topics.title: Theme I: Responsible consumption and conservation

subtopics.title: Energy of raw vs recycled materials

outcomes.text: Compare the energy required to use raw materials versus recycled materials.

topics.title: Theme II: Renewable energy use

outcomes.text: Cite evidence of how rapid economic growth and industrial expansion raise energy use, pollution and climate change.
Explain reliance on non-renewable energy as a cause of that harm.

topics.title: Theme III: Water management

outcomes.text: Measure rainfall and safely observe river and well levels at home, keeping records.
Explain what water security means.

topics.title: Theme IV: Sustainable lifestyle

outcomes.text: Define carbon footprint in simple terms.

topics.title: Theme I: Social impacts of climate change

outcomes.text: Understand what climate crises occur in different provinces of Pakistan and how they affect people.

topics.title: Theme II: Strategies for safety and resilience

outcomes.text: Prepare a list of steps to take after a natural disaster.
Identify the roles community and youth can play in emergency response.

topics.title: Theme III: Climate anxiety and constructive coping

outcomes.text: Research the emotions people may have after climate loss and damage to families and assets.

topics.title: Theme IV: Community action

outcomes.text: Apply critical thinking to assess school climate action plans that guide policy and practice to meet climate targets.

topics.title: Theme I: Economic growth and development

outcomes.text: Analyse how economic activities (industry, transport, agriculture) affect the environment and climate.
Discuss waste management challenges, including recycling and landfills locally.
Categorise natural resources consumed in production.
Estimate resource use such as water and energy and suggest ways to conserve.
Analyse sustainability actions such as calculating carbon footprints.

topics.title: Theme II: Carbon credits and carbon markets

outcomes.text: Describe the carbon cycle: sinks, sources and the role of ecosystems.
Define carbon emissions, their natural and human sources, and their role in the greenhouse effect.
Estimate carbon output of human activities such as transport choices and suggest ways to cut footprint.

topics.title: Theme III: Circular economy

outcomes.text: Classify types of waste and trace the journey of waste to landfill, recycling or incineration.
Explain the 4Rs (Refuse/Reduce, Repair, Reuse, Recycle) and their hierarchy.
Conduct a waste audit at school or home.
Calculate the percentage of waste that can be reduced, reused or recycled and track improvement.

topics.title: Theme IV: Green and blue economy

outcomes.text: Explain the blue economy as the responsible use of ocean and river resources.
Explain the green economy in simple terms and its link to sustainability and development.

topics.title: Theme I: Our environment

outcomes.text: Discuss how humans shape and impact their natural environments.

topics.title: Theme II: Biodiversity

outcomes.text: Describe the evolutionary process as a long journey.
Describe how living things today adapt to changing conditions.

topics.title: Theme III: Human relation to the natural environment

outcomes.text: Identify various types of pollution: air, soil, water, light and noise.
Research how people living in cities can stay connected to nature.

topics.title: Theme I: Causes of climate change

outcomes.text: Explore how electricity is generated and which ways use fossil fuel and add carbon to the atmosphere.
Identify ways industries and transport add carbon.

topics.title: Theme II: Climate change impacts and hazards

outcomes.text: Describe the concepts of adaptation and mitigation.
Search for adaptation methods for a local climate crisis.
Discuss tools and technologies that help mitigate climate change.

topics.title: Theme III: Monitoring climate change

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the methods of Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) and the tools used.
Recognise why an EIA is needed before starting a project.

topics.title: Theme IV: Climate justice

outcomes.text: Assess how climate injustice is a problem.
Draw lessons from history about people with power who depleted resources without thinking of future generations.

topics.title: Theme I: Responsible consumption and conservation

outcomes.text: Investigate the role of sustainable farming practices in reducing environmental footprints.

topics.title: Theme II: Renewable energy use

outcomes.text: Explain with examples that energy efficiency is an important climate mitigation approach.
Compare national or international innovations for energy conservation and efficiency.

topics.title: Theme III: Water management

outcomes.text: Assess the relevance of water purification methods: chlorination, sedimentation, filtration, evaporation, desalination.
Research national water policies and how well they ensure water security in Pakistan.

topics.title: Theme IV: Sustainable lifestyle

outcomes.text: Analyse the relationship between diet and health.

topics.title: Theme I: Social impacts of climate change

outcomes.text: Compare the climate impact on a rich developed country and a poor developing country, including social aspects.

topics.title: Theme II: Strategies for safety and resilience

subtopics.title: Reducing risk at home and school

outcomes.text: Brainstorm actions to reduce harmful risks in the home or classroom, such as sandbags and cooling strategies.

topics.title: Theme III: Climate anxiety and constructive coping

outcomes.text: Develop a basic understanding of the healing process with help from teachers and elders.

topics.title: Theme IV: Community action

outcomes.text: Assess whether municipal or local community leaders are urgently taking climate action.

topics.title: Theme I: Economic growth and development

outcomes.text: Recognise that industries generate different types of waste and their impact.
Compare composting methods from an urban versus rural view.
Discuss the impact of resource extraction on ecosystems and communities.
Track and classify household waste and propose reduction, reuse and recycling methods.
Measure resource consumption such as water and energy and suggest responsible use.

topics.title: Theme II: Carbon credits and carbon markets

outcomes.text: Define carbon credits, their purpose and how they offset emissions.
Identify strategies for reducing emissions: renewables, afforestation, sustainable transport.
Research real examples of carbon credit projects.

topics.title: Theme III: Circular economy

outcomes.text: Compare linear and circular economies using a Venn diagram.
Explore waste used as a resource: composting, upcycling, waste-to-energy.
Classify everyday products as linear or circular and propose waste repurposing projects.

topics.title: Theme IV: Green and blue economy

outcomes.text: Analyse how the blue economy balances growth, livelihoods and aquatic ecosystem health.
Compare blue economy challenges and opportunities in coastal areas versus river systems.

topics.title: Theme I: Our environment

outcomes.text: Describe large fluxes of matter in a specific ecosystem, such as carbon and nitrogen moving through a food web.
Explain carbon, phosphorus and nitrate cycles between biosphere, atmosphere and lithosphere.
Describe small-scale fluxes and energy changes such as in cellular respiration.
Understand middle-scale energy fluxes in an organism.
Show complex thinking about biodiversity.

topics.title: Theme II: Biodiversity

outcomes.text: Give specific examples of species diversity and endangered species such as birds, bees and frogs.
Discuss how some animal and plant species became extinct and what changes in their ecosystem caused it.

topics.title: Theme III: Human relation to the natural environment

outcomes.text: Describe how buildings, towns and cities have less biodiversity than natural areas.

topics.title: Theme I: Causes of climate change

outcomes.text: Investigate why carbon is a hazardous element and how it causes climate change.
Make a simple computation of a carbon footprint.

topics.title: Theme II: Climate change impacts and hazards

outcomes.text: Clarify why international cooperation is needed to reduce climate change.
Explain the importance of government engagement in climate action.
List national and international organisations working on climate change.
Discuss how youth are represented at climate forums.

topics.title: Theme III: Monitoring climate change

outcomes.text: Demonstrate energy audit methods and tools used.
Demonstrate how carbon footprint is measured and the tools used.
Understand carbon credits and conduct an energy audit at home.

topics.title: Theme IV: Climate justice

outcomes.text: Identify a role they can play in addressing the unfair impacts of climate change.
Argue with evidence that fossil fuel transition is needed for climate justice.

topics.title: Theme I: Responsible consumption and conservation

outcomes.text: Analyse how air, water and land pollution affect local communities in Pakistan.
Investigate how the 4Rs can be built into industries and businesses to promote sustainability.

topics.title: Theme II: Renewable energy use

outcomes.text: Explain how technological innovation drives the growth of renewable energy, such as better solar and wind efficiency.
Research how technology also causes climate change and so should be used with the 4Rs.

topics.title: Theme III: Water management

outcomes.text: Explain the concept of rainwater harvesting.
Research and present rainwater harvesting methods for schools, houses and public places.
Explain why conserving water matters with dams, Karez, storage tanks and recharge wells.

topics.title: Theme IV: Sustainable lifestyle

outcomes.text: Identify the principles of energy conservation and their connection to zero-energy homes.

topics.title: Theme I: Social impacts of climate change

outcomes.text: Identify opportunities for collaboration between developed and less developed countries on climate change and its benefits.

topics.title: Theme II: Strategies for safety and resilience

outcomes.text: Investigate changes needed in infrastructure, systems, lifestyles and the economy to build resilience and adapt.
Research local and international organisations working on emergency preparedness and response.

topics.title: Theme III: Climate anxiety and constructive coping

outcomes.text: Analyse the philosophy behind safety first during emergencies and disasters.
Discuss strategies to maintain self-control and regulate emotions to help self and others in a disaster.

topics.title: Theme IV: Community action

outcomes.text: Assess whether national and subnational climate policy aligns with international targets such as cutting emissions 45% by 2030.
Analyse policies for youth participation and leadership in climate action.

topics.title: Theme I: Economic growth and development

outcomes.text: Differentiate economic growth from development using real-world examples.
Explain principles of sustainable development, including resource conservation, renewable energy and equitable growth, in Pakistan.
Present case studies of sustainable industrial practices, using statistics and charts.

topics.title: Theme II: Carbon credits and carbon markets

outcomes.text: Identify international agreements like the Paris Agreement, COP meetings and Pakistan's national action steps.
Explain technological and economic pathways to a zero-carbon economy.
Understand green jobs and emerging green technologies such as solar technicians and carbon capture engineering.
Propose innovative solutions for a zero-carbon future and design a green technology model.

topics.title: Theme III: Circular economy

outcomes.text: Explain the environmental impact of man-made products using basic life cycle assessment.
Explain how sharing makes the economy more sustainable and calculate material savings.
Compare the environmental impact of products such as plastic versus cloth bags.
Evaluate how a rapidly growing population affects a country's economic development.

topics.title: Theme IV: Green and blue economy

subtopics.title: Sectors of blue and green economies

outcomes.text: Investigate blue economy sectors: offshore renewable energy, sustainable fisheries, green shipping, marine tourism, aquaculture.
Describe green economy sectors: renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, eco-tourism.
Propose solutions to blue economy challenges such as overfishing and marine and river pollution.
Design and carry out a community green initiative and debate energy sources.
